data.name: Tripura
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Tripura refers to the three cities built by the demon king, Tripura Asura. Tripura is often depicted as a symbol of power and destruction. The gods, led by Lord Shiva, finally destroy the cities to restore peace and order.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of destruction and the eventual attainment of peace.

vedic_reference.note: In Hindu mythology, Tripura refers to the three cities of the Asuras (demons). These cities were created by the Asura king, Mahasur, and were protected by his three daughters, Tripura Sundari, Tripura Bhairavi, and Tripura Triyambaka.

data.cultural_impact: Tripura is a name deeply engrained in Hindu mythology, representing the important narrative of the battle between good and evil. The story of Tripura highlights the significance of courage, righteousness, and the power of unity to overcome evil forces. It is also depicted in various forms of Indian art and literature.
data.spiritual_significance: Tripura represents the idea of overcoming internal and external sources of negativity and evil through the power of spiritual growth and the unity of the divine. The name symbolizes the journey towards peace,order and spiritual liberation as depicted in the Hindu scripture. Additionally, Tripura prayers are believed to grant protection against negative energies.

historical_references.reference: The legend of Tripura tells the story of a demon king named Tripura, who was invincible due to the boon he received from Brahma that he could not be destroyed by any god. This angered the gods, who decided to seek the help of the god Shiva.

The Tripura region in the northeastern part of India was a significant center of the ancient Indian kingdom of Tripura, which is believed to have existed from the 7th century AD to the 16th century AD. The region was ruled by the Tripura kings, who were considered to be descendants of the god Shiva and claimed divine descent.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Tripura' has gained significant modern context across various platforms. In social media, there are numerous groups and pages dedicated to the Tripura Sundari Temple, a famous Hindu shrine located in Tripura, India. The temple is considered one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and is known for its rich history and architectural significance. On the tourism industry platform, Tripura is marketed as a popular tourist destination in India, especially for its religious and cultural significance. Lastly, in religious and cultural events, Tripura Raja and Tripura Balabhadra are revered deities, and various rituals and festivals are dedicated to them.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Tripura signifies the three cities of the goddess Durga, symbolizing her cosmic power over creation, preservation, and destruction. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'tripura' meaning 'three cities' and 'sundari' meaning 'beautiful.' Thus, Tripura embodies the divine feminine, representing both destructive and creative aspects of the universe.
